summary.headline: Paradeep Phosphates Q1 FY27 revenue rose 36% YoY to Rs.6,124 crore, with EBITDA of Rs.742 crore and about Rs.7,000/t EBITDA per tonne.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations rose 36% YoY to Rs.6,124 crore, EBITDA rose 21% to Rs.742 crore, PBT rose 24% to Rs.526 crore and PAT stood at Rs.393 crore. Sales volume grew 4% to 9.85 lakh tonnes, with sulphuric acid output up 32% and phosphoric acid output up 7% YoY as backward integration benefits came through. Management said Q1 EBITDA per tonne was helped by low-cost opening inventory and guided to a sustainable Rs.5,000/t for the year. The board approved a Rs.250 crore aluminium fluoride plant (15,000 tpa) to diversify into non-subsidy industrial chemicals. Management flagged Middle East-driven volatility and availability issues in sulphur and ammonia as the key near-term risk.

financial_highlights.change: vs about Rs.6,500/t in Q1 FY26 and about Rs.5,300/t in Q4 FY26

financial_highlights.value: about Rs.2,650 crore (Rs.2,600 crore cited in a question)
financial_highlights.change: subsidy collections 22% higher YoY per management
debt reduced by about Rs.700 crore overall per management

segments.name: DAP
segments.commentary: Volumes up about 55% YoY in Q1, driven by better profitability under the current policy; Q1 traded DAP was only about 1,000 tonnes because most DAP was manufactured in-house.

segments.name: NPK
segments.commentary: Volumes down about 9% YoY, while farmer sales grew about 6%; a significant price increase was taken to protect profitability.

segments.name: Traded products
segments.commentary: Q1 traded volumes were about 1.25 lakh tonnes (incl. MOP, TSP, DAP); TSP about 24,000 t and ammonium sulphate about 22,000 t. About 5 lakh tonnes of imports secured for rabi, arriving July to September.

segments.name: Urea (Goa/Mangalore)
segments.commentary: Goa G-Cal improvement of 0.2 gives about Rs.1,000/t benefit; management said a normalised EBITDA uplift of about Rs.700-800/t is valid for Q1 FY27 at Goa. New urea policy expected to add about Rs.1,500/t at Goa and reduce Mangalore by about Rs.700-800/t.

segments.name: Aluminium fluoride (proposed)
segments.commentary: Rs.250 crore plant at Paradeep, 15,000 tpa capacity, expected top line Rs.180-200 crore and EBITDA of at least Rs.50 crore; commissioning in 22-24 months. Current hydrofluorosilicic acid (FSA) production of 9,000-10,000 tpa is sold to third parties.

guidance_outlook: Sustainable EBITDA guidance of Rs.5,000/t for the year; management expects to cross this by year end if coordination with government works, and said there is no pressure on EBITDA/t below guidance despite higher trading volumes.
Management said Rs.7,000/t plus sustainable EBITDA can come after expansions, in phases over about 2 to 2.5 years.

Phosphoric acid expansion phase I (5 lakh to 6 lakh t) by December 2026; a further 1 lakh t (to 7 lakh t) by about August-September 2026; a bigger 3 lakh t phosphoric plus sulphuric acid expansion of about Rs.3,500-3,600 crore in one shot around FY29-30.
Granulation debottlenecking from 3.7 to 4 (units not specified) expected by December 2026; contract awarded.
Long-term target: at least 20% of EBITDA from non-subsidy business, which will take time to evolve.
Traded volumes in rabi to be significantly higher than last year (last year rabi about 2.7 lakh t); no exact number guided.
capex_capacity: Phosphoric acid expansion phase I from 5 lakh t to 6 lakh t on track for December 2026; execution under way with equipment ordered. Phase II to 7 lakh t expected around August-September 2026.
Management said phosphoric acid plant utilisation is almost 100%.
Sulphuric acid capacity expanded at Paradeep from 1.4 to 2 million tonnes; sulphuric acid output up 32% YoY in Q1 and capacity fully utilised with no outside sales.
Aluminium fluoride plant: Rs.250 crore, 15,000 tpa; board approved in Q1 FY27; engineering started; commissioning in 22-24 months.

Larger Rs.3,500-3,600 crore phosphoric acid and sulphuric acid expansion to be commissioned in one shot around FY29-30 (management said around Q2 FY29 for early elements). Management said NPK granulation and expansion plans are unchanged.
demand_pricing: Farmer sales growth of about 15-16% in Q1 versus industry phosphatic (DAP and NPK) growth of about 1%, per management.

Management said DAP demand is robust at the government-set price; NPK is priced at Rs.2,100-2,500/bag for complexes versus DAP at Rs.1,350/bag, a gap of about Rs.1,000/bag. Management said DAP and NPK prices within Rs.200/bag would let farmers shift back quickly.
Industry phosphate market about 24 million t: DAP about 10 million t, NPK about 14 million t, of which the 20:20:0:13 grade is about 6-7 million t.
Sulphur averaged about $850/t in Q1 and is now $1,000+/t; sulphuric acid is now $350-370/t. No long-term sulphur contracts; all procurement is spot.
Management said about 70-75% of global sulphur and ammonia trade passes through the Strait of Hormuz, and supply disruptions are expected to continue in the short term.
Monsoon was a concern, but July rainfall has been good.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NPK volumes fall 9% while DAP rose 55%, and will this mix hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said DAP is the profitability-led focus under current policy, NPK farmer sales still grew about 6%, and a significant NPK price increase was passed partly to farmers.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Rs.7,000/t EBITDA per tonne in Q1 sustain?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 benefited from low-cost opening inventory; realistic annual EBITDA is about Rs.5,000/t, rising to Rs.7,000+/t after expansions in phases over 2-2.5 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity and cash flow position?
qa_highlights.answer: Subsidy outstanding about Rs.4,600 crore at 30 June, with about Rs.2,650 crore received in the year; gross debt Rs.6,500 crore; management said operating cash flow is positive and debt down about Rs.700 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What are the phosphoric acid and bigger capex timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase I 1 lakh t by December 2026, further 1 lakh t by August-September 2026, and a Rs.3,500-3,600 crore one-shot expansion around FY29-30; timelines unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: Will traded volumes hurt margins in rabi?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give exact rabi trading volumes, said they will be significantly higher than last year, and said EBITDA/t guidance is maintained at company level.

qa_highlights.question: Is the DAP price cap likely to be removed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a matter for the government and does not seem likely in the short term, but it should be removed at some point.

risks_watch: Sulphur and ammonia supply and price volatility from the Middle East conflict; no long-term sulphur contracts in place.
Subsidy receivable of about Rs.4,600 crore and dependence on government support for cost increases.
Policy-driven DAP/NPK price gap that could slow the NPK shift; management said NPK recovery is quick if the gap narrows.
Phosphoric acid utilisation near 100% limits upside until the December 2026 and August-September 2026 expansion steps.
Traded-volume mix in rabi may dilute margins; management said EBITDA/t guidance is still held.
Execution risk on the Rs.250 crore aluminium fluoride plant (22-24 months) and the Rs.3,500-3,600 crore FY29-30 expansion.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operating and financial delivery, with explicit caution on the Middle East supply shock and raw material volatility. Management was more guarded on pricing and policy, and on the timing of DAP price reform, which it said is for government to decide.
key_quotes: PPL has once again delivered a very strong financial and operational performance and the best-in-class EBITDA per ton.
we cannot be just sticking to what exactly we have done. So, this is a small-term tactical shift which is going to come.
Any shortage in the production will be made good by this trading. So, overall there will be no decrease in the sales and other things.
we do not see any challenge in terms of the marketability or saleability of this product.
